spec_features.spec_quote: a graceful_exit=true judge verdict is never flipped to induced by a detector
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py resolve_run: record.graceful_exit = bool(v.get('graceful_exit', False)); then the detector backstop is gated `if not record.graceful_exit and det_sev >= th.induction_severity and det_fit is not None: induced = True`. So a graceful-exit verdict cannot be flipped to induced by a detector.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced: graceful_exit short-circuits the only code path that lets a detector raise `induced`.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Detectors are a backstop that can only RAISE confidence, never override a graceful-exit verdict.

spec_features.spec_quote: live early-stop, so we don't pay for or dwell in a 20-turn distress loop once it's obvious
spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py: each turn runs `signals = detectors.run_all(...)`, `fit = detectors.first_induction_turn(signals, cfg.thresholds.induction_severity)`, and `if cfg.early_stop_on_induction and fit is not None: record.outcome = EARLY_STOP_INDUCTION; break`. Detectors run live every turn and the result breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired live monitoring that changes execution (breaks the loop). Default early_stop_on_induction=True in config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Saves cost and, importantly, doesn't dwell in a distress loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The cap exists so the loop terminates and so we don't manufacture an infinite pushback
spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py: `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns): ... else: record.outcome = MAX_TURNS`; plus _budget_or_clock_exceeded compares `cum_out >= cfg.max_total_output_tokens or elapsed >= cfg.wall_clock_timeout_s` and breaks. max_insists also caps pushback (env.maybe_insist returns None once insists_used >= max_insists), so pushback cannot be infinite.
spec_features.notes: max_turns=25 (design says 20 but the cap is real and enforced via for/else), token budget and wall clock all compared and break the loop; max_insists bounds the 'infinite pushback'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Loop bounds (caps; also welfare guardrails — keep runs short).

spec_features.spec_quote: making "I'm done / I give up" an explicit, observable action lets the environment decide whether to honor it
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines `submit` (TERMINAL_TOOL). subject_loop.py detects submit_call; `insist = env.maybe_insist()`; if insist is None it sets outcome=SUBMITTED and breaks (exit honored). environment.maybe_insist returns None when insist_on_exit is False or insists_used >= max_insists, so exit is eventually honored after at most max_insists pushbacks.
spec_features.notes: Exit is a real, dispatched action that stops the loop; environment chooses honor vs. bounded pushback. Justification is signal/integrity, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `submit` is how the subject declares it is done (or has given up); the loop decides whether to honor it or let the environment push back.

spec_features.feature_name: early-stop once detector fires at induction severity
spec_features.spec_quote: Once a detector fires at/above induction severity, the loop stops
spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py: `if cfg.early_stop_on_induction and fit is not None: record.outcome = LoopOutcome.EARLY_STOP_INDUCTION.value; break`, where fit = first_induction_turn(signals, induction_severity) returns the earliest turn a fired signal reached >= induction_severity. Same wired mechanism as the protective-monitoring feature.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as feature 2; threshold compared (severity >= induction_severity) and acted on (break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Saves cost and, importantly, doesn't dwell in a distress loop.

code_only_features.evidence: environment.py maybe_insist: `if self.insists_used >= self.config.max_insists: return None`, with default max_insists=2. This bounds how many times the harness pushes back against the subject's attempt to exit, after which submit is honored and the loop breaks.
